text:
Posted by Nicole Wilson on Apr 26th, 2018 // No Comments
Graybill Bartz & Assoc Ltd. trimmed its stake in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 11.8% during the fourth quarter, according to its most recent disclosure with the SEC. The fund owned 31,759 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 4,260 shares during the quarter. Apple makes up about 3.9% of Graybill Bartz & Assoc Ltd.’s investment portfolio, making the stock its largest holding. Graybill Bartz & Assoc Ltd.’s holdings in Apple were worth $5,375,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Several other hedge funds and other institutional investors also recently modified their holdings of AAPL. CWM LLC grew its holdings in Apple by 8.4% during the fourth quarter. CWM LLC now owns 75,219 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $12,729,000 after acquiring an additional 5,858 shares during the period. Baltimore Washington Financial Advisors Inc. grew its holdings in Apple by 94.2% during the fourth quarter. Baltimore Washington Financial Advisors Inc. now owns 132,103 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $22,354,000 after acquiring an additional 64,080 shares during the period. Whalerock Point Partners LLC grew its holdings in Apple by 7.0% during the fourth quarter. Whalerock Point Partners LLC now owns 58,820 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $9,955,000 after acquiring an additional 3,866 shares during the period. Strategic Advisors LLC grew its holdings in Apple by 2.0% during the fourth quarter. Strategic Advisors LLC now owns 63,208 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $10,697,000 after acquiring an additional 1,226 shares during the period. Finally, Convergence Investment Partners LLC grew its holdings in Apple by 1.3% during the fourth quarter. Convergence Investment Partners LLC now owns 48,902 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $8,276,000 after acquiring an additional 623 shares during the period. Institutional investors and hedge funds own 61.28% of the company’s stock.
Shares of AAPL traded up $0.71 on Wednesday, reaching $163.65. 28,289,920 shares of the stock traded hands, compared to its average volume of 36,220,535. The stock has a market cap of $838,429.94, a PE ratio of 17.77, a P/E/G ratio of 1.26 and a beta of 1.25. The company has a current ratio of 1.24, a quick ratio of 1.20 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74. Apple has a 12 month low of $142.20 and a 12 month high of $183.50.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its quarterly earnings data on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, beating analysts’ consensus estimates of $3.82 by $0.07. Apple had a return on equity of 37.37% and a net margin of 21.13%. The business had revenue of $88.29 billion for the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $87.62 billion. During the same period in the previous year, the business posted $3.36 earnings per share. Apple’s quarterly revenue was up 12.7% on a year-over-year basis. equities analysts forecast that Apple will post 11.3 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
A number of research analysts recently issued reports on the company. Nomura reaffirmed a “neutral” rating and set a $175.00 target price on shares of Apple in a report on Monday, March 19th. BidaskClub cut Apple from a “hold” rating to a “sell” rating in a research note on Friday, January 26th. BMO Capital Markets cut Apple from an “outperform” rating to a “market perform” rating and lifted their price target for the stock from $162.00 to $166.00 in a research note on Wednesday, January 31st. William Blair reissued an “outperform” rating on shares of Apple in a research note on Friday, February 2nd. Finally, Bank of America reissued an “outperform” rating and issued a $220.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research note on Thursday, February 8th. Two investment analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have issued a hold rating, thirty-two have assigned a buy rating and one has assigned a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. Apple currently has an average rating of “Buy” and an average price target of $203.15.
In other Apple news, SVP Daniel J. Riccio sold 17,375 shares of the company’s stock in a transaction on Wednesday, April 4th. The stock was sold at an average price of $169.12, for a total value of $2,938,460.00. Following the sale, the senior vice president now directly owns 66,191 shares in the company, valued at $11,194,221.92. The sale was disclosed in a document filed with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is accessible through this hyperlink . Also, insider Luca Maestri sold 39,122 shares of the company’s stock in a transaction on Friday, April 13th. The shares were sold at an average price of $174.66, for a total value of $6,833,048.52. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now owns 64,475 shares in the company, valued at $11,261,203.50. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders sold 125,988 shares of company stock worth $21,336,201 over the last quarter. Company insiders own 0.06% of the company’s stock. Apple Company Profile
Apple Inc (Apple) designs, manufactures and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, and portable digital music players, and a variety of related software, services, peripherals, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications. The Company’s products and services include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple TV, a portfolio of consumer and professional software applications, the iOS and OS X operating systems, iCloud, and a variety of accessory, service and support offerings.
